The Diel.Niche classification (Methods: cathemeral, diurnal, crepuscular or nocturnal from the proportions of observations in daytime, nighttime and twilight) labels the brown hyena cathemeral: the Results sentence gives 64.5% nocturnal and 22.6% diurnal detections and classifies brown hyena and leopard (31% and 55.2%) each as cathemeral. The Discussion says brown hyenas are more active during dark hours, confirming earlier studies that call the species nocturnal, and that the proportion of daylight activity nonetheless classifies it as cathemeral.
